tone.says: Syllable C(C)V(V)T with 'seven or eight (depending on the dialect) lexical tones' (p. 6); breathiness distinguishes some categories (p. 8). Table (6) p. 12 'Phonetic realisation of PM tones': Shuat A1 55, A2 41, B1 53, C1 44, D1 33, B2 22 (breathy), C2 33 (breathy), D2 21 - no mergers, i.e. Shuat keeps all eight Proto-Miao categories, whereas Dleub, Soud, Bes, Buak, Shib, E Nzhuab show mergers (7 tones; Buak a ninth breathy tone); (11) p. 15 descriptive labels (Shuat A1 high level, B1 high fall…

sources.note: First-hand phonological sketch with a 'Tones' section and a 'Tone Sandhi' section. Syllable = initial + rime + tone ('a phonologically contrastive prosody of pitch and phonation'). All eight Farwestern-Hmongic tone categories retained: /1/ [45]~[55] (b), /2/ [31]~[21] (x), /3/ [53] (d), /4/ [22] breathy (l), /5/ [44]~[34] (t), /6/ [33] breathy (s), /7/ [22] modal (k), /8/ [11] often glottalised, ~[12]~[23] phrase-finally (f); tones 4 and 6 have identical level contours with breathy phonation and differ only in pitch height; tones 5 and 7 both approach [33] but stay distinct in minimal pairs.…
